Hi Priya and Daniel,

Thanks — great questions. High level answers up front, then I9ll loop in engineering for a short ops-level runbook and diagram.

1) Control plane: We offer a private control plane option that can be deployed customer-managed inside a VPC (recommended for regulated banks). That control plane stores only metadata and orchestration state; customer data paths (inference payloads, KV cache) remain on customer-hosted GPUs or dedicated instances in the selected region.

2) Data residency: Logs and metrics can be routed to your EU KMS-backed storage (S3 with SSE-KMS) when running in EU region. For APAC we can direct to your APAC bucket. KV cache and model state never leave the regional deployment unless you explicitly enable cross-region replication.

3) Failover options & SLOs: We support both active-passive (recommended for strict residency) and active-active (if you can accept cross-region replication of model caches). Typical active-passive RTO is 10-15 minutes for service rehydration with warm standby; RPO is near-zero for metadata (control plane replication), but KV cache rebuild time depends on model size and can be up to 30 minutes without pre-warmed caches. We9ll include a warm-standby checklist.

4) Networking: Minimum requirements: site-to-site VPN or Direct Connect/ExpressRoute equivalent between your VPCs and Redwood management plane, a pair of egress IPs per region for allowlisting, and optional BGP for automated failover. We9ll provide a concrete port/IP list.

I9m attaching an ops sketch and a short checklist. Can we schedule a 45-minute call Thurs (12th) or Mon (16th) to walk the Finova ops and legal teams through the plan?

Thanks,
Evelyn Hart

Eve / Marissa — technical notes below (ops-oriented). I9ll prepare a one-pager for the call.

Proposed topology (recommended):
- Separate regional deployments: EU cluster (Ireland data center) and APAC cluster (Singapore). Each region runs inference nodes + local KV caches.
- Customer-managed private control plane: deployed via CloudFormation/Terraform in customer VPC, with mutual-TLS to regional runtimes. Control plane holds metadata only and is configured per region.
- Warm-standby failover: standby cluster in target region with pre-pulled model artifacts but limited serving capacity to keep costs down. On failover we promote the standby and re-route traffic via DNS weight shift (TTL 30s) + BGP route failover if available.

Data flows & residency guarantees:
- Inference requests from EU customers terminate in EU runtime; logs and metrics flush to EU KMS-protected bucket. No KV cache checkpoint replication to APAC in baseline configuration.
- If customer permits cross-region replication for faster failover (active-active), we encrypt KV snapshots with customer KMS and push over an encrypted channel; this requires explicit config and acceptance in the contract.

RTO/RPO estimates (empirical):
- Control plane failover (metadata replication): RPO ~0s, RTO ~2-5 minutes (leader election + service handoff).
- Standby promotion (warm standby): RPO ~0-5 minutes for metadata, KV cache RPO depends on snapshot cadence (we recommend 5 min cadence if they want sub-10min cache recovery). Full throughput restoration typically 10-20 minutes depending on model size and GPU availability.

Networking checklist (short):
- Site-to-site VPN or private interconnect (Direct Connect / ExpressRoute).
- Static egress IPs for Redwood management endpoints per region (we'll provide a list).
- Open outbound ports: 443, 8443 (for mutual-TLS), 9090 (metrics push) — full list in attached network-checklist.xlsx.
- Optional: BGP + health probes for automatic path failover.

Security / Compliance docs to share quickly:
- soc2-summary.pdf (iso summary)
- Encryption-at-rest & KMS integration notes (I'll hand over an integration doc)

Operational runbook (high level):
1) Pre-deploy: confirm VPC peering, KMS key ARNs, and egress allowlist.
2) Deploy control plane in EU and APAC VPCs.
3) Deploy regional runtimes and pre-pull model artifacts onto warm-standby nodes.
4) Configure monitoring alerts and failover playbook (DNS weight shift + manual promotion).
5) Run DR test once per quarter.

I9ll attach a concise diagram and a granular playbook for the call.
